analysis.title: Nomura Quant Insights: Post-midterm election period and AI sell-off: Signs of overshooting and limited upside / Increase in hedge fund redemptions
key_insights: Global AI reversal accelerated last week after the midterm election surprise ("blue tsunami"). The Nasdaq at one point fell roughly 15% from its recent high, and moves increasingly resembled a panic sell-off.
The VIX surged as cross-stock correlations rose. The term structure shows backwardation on a scale not seen since the start of the Iran war.
Semiconductor implied volatility exceeded the highs from the July AI stock sell-off. Nomura sees limited risk of further correction in the short term.

Nikkei 225 options: peak short gamma is broadly around 58,000. The short interest factor in Japanese equities had its strongest outperformance of the post-pandemic era, and last Thursday was likely painful for long/short investors.

The bottom-up Nikkei 225 target return has surged above 40%, similar to the Covid crash, yen carry meltdown and tariff shock. Nomura does not expect an immediate V-shaped recovery like the one after the yen carry meltdown.

Political uncertainty over data center construction is unlikely to clear until the new Congress convenes in January, so target returns are likely to stay at risk-off levels (above 30%). Nomura's year-end Nikkei 225 rebound target is 64,000.

Retail margin trading is a supply-demand risk. Based on August 2024, forced liquidations could easily exceed ¥1trn. There is little evidence of large-scale stop-loss selling last week, and the margin-imbalance factor's underperformance has not accelerated.

CTAs' aggregate net short in the Nikkei 225 is around ¥1trn (Nomura model estimate), with room to expand by roughly ¥500bn to a tariff-shock scale. If prices recover to 63,000, these shorts could be covered rapidly.

Globally, investors may be late to exit. CTA S&P 500 positions are down 80% from their peak but still net long, and volatility control funds have room to cut long exposure further. Nomura sees a Nikkei 225 floor in the 54,000-55,000 range.

A short-term rebound in AI-related shares would not be surprising, and the Nvidia event premium in US index options is no longer conspicuous. Nomura does not expect a major rebound in AI momentum itself.

Hedge fund redemptions are expanding. Funds that struggled this year are likely to see more outflows into year-end, and some funds are reportedly already meeting redemption requests. Year-to-date returns have turned negative on some major platforms, and equity hedge fund excess returns over the risk-free rate are negative.

Thirty days is the most common redemption notice period among equity hedge funds, and few require 45 days. It is premature to assume redemption-related selling finished last week. Fund outflows in Oct-Dec tend to weaken momentum.

Oil and bonds are near-term rotation catalysts. The oil normalization priced in oil options and bonds has become reality. If non-spot markets keep leading, oil could fall a further roughly $15, and the lower Middle East escalation risk makes a return toward recent lows unsurprising.
Falling oil may trigger short covering in sectors hit hardest by the Iran war, such as automobiles and real estate, which rallied sharply last Thursday.

Yields have fallen alongside the AI reversal, and investors increasingly focus on a December 2018-style risk-off with equities down and bonds up. The December FOMC carries the largest event premium in Treasury options, with skew tilted toward calls.

The market is unsure how Chair Warsh will read the AI stock decline and is waiting for the FOMC. If it passes without incident, the yield decline is expected to resume. CTAs lean toward selling equities and buying bonds, and bond shorts have been reduced only modestly.

sector_views.rationale: Shorts in these sectors, most affected by the Iran war, are likely to be covered as crude falls. They rallied sharply last Thursday.
Implied volatility exceeded July highs. A short-term bounce is possible, but Nomura expects no major rebound in AI momentum and sees rotation away from AI over the longer term.

earnings_insights: Event premium assigned to mid-November tech stock results is not conspicuous in S&P 500 options (Fig. 7).
